queer_characters.name: Dr. Shrinivas Ramchandra Siras
queer_characters.notes: Based on the true story of a real gay professor; film depicts a consensual intimate moment with a man and centers his persecution under Section 377, described as a rare, dignified portrait of the Indian gay male experience and of loneliness.

contributor_notes: Siras's gay identity is central and explicit in the film's premise (filmed in an intimate moment with a man, prosecuted under Section 377). His tragic death is part of the real historical events, so 'tragic-queer' is flagged as historical-context rather than gratuitous — a maintainer may wish to reconsider whether 'bury-your-gays' applies given the true-story basis. 'own-voices' community tag is a guess about the source text describing this as authentic to the Indian gay experience — please verify, as no creator identity is stated in the source. Deepak Sebastian (journalist) and director Hansal Mehta have no queerness indicated in the source and were not tagged. Subtitles/audio languages not mentioned in source.
